stories.title: Gunmen kill at least 10 villagers and loot shops in north-east Nigeria
stories.summary: Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, File image of Nigerian police officers By Timothy Obiezu ,Â West Africa producer, Â and Â Patrick Jackson Published 6 hours ago Unknown gunmen have raided a remote village in the north-eastern Nigerian state of Taraba, killing at least 10 people, looting shops and setting houses ablaze, police say. There are fears the actual death toll is much higher, with eyewitnesses speaking of 20 lives lost and a non-governmental organisation suggesting a toll of as many as 50. The gunmen reportedly swooped on the village of Binnari in the Karim Lamido area mounted on motorcycles just after midday Muslim prayers on Friday in a rampage that went on for up to four hours. Police say they are searching for other casualties in the bush but the authorities were accused by Amnesty International of failing to protect rural communities. Nigeria continues to face attacks by armed groups across several regions, including the northwest, northeast and central regions.

Dozens of builders had been working on the upper floors when it collapsed, but managed to emerge largely unscathed. Those missing were thought to have been in shops at the base of the building. The incident has raised fresh concerns about construction standards and regulations in Kenya.

" If we lift the foot off the pedal, the virus will resurge very quickly, will continue to spread to newly affected areas and pose a threat for the country, the region and the world at large ," warned Dr. Catherine Smallwood, World Health Organization ( WHO ) incident manager in the DRC. stories.title: Africa: 'Too Arrogant, Too Sure of Itself' France Confronts Its Legacy in Africa
stories.summary: Africa: 'Too Arrogant, Too Sure of Itself' France Confronts Its Legacy in Africa 23 October 2026 Radio France Internationale By Alison Hird Fifteen years after France promised a new relationship with Africa, Paris is still struggling to reconcile its rejection of colonial-era interference with its desire to retain influence on the continent. RFI Africa specialist Christophe Boisbouvier argues in a new book that France can still build a partnership of equals - based on respect rather than arrogance or domination. "Too arrogant, too sure of itself, France failed to see the anti-French wave coming," Boisbouvier says. His book, Françafrique Is Dead, Long Live Africa-France , examines the breakdown of France's old model of relations with the continent. For decades after African countries gained independence, Paris maintained privileged relationships with friendly leaders and sought to protect its strategic interests - sometimes through military intervention. The system, known as Françafrique , gradually became synonymous with a neo-colonial pattern of French influence and patronage.

stories.title: Paddy Donnelly obituary
stories.summary: Paddy Donnelly came to London from South Africa in the early 80s to work for the International Defence and Aid Fund for Southern Africa View image in fullscreen Paddy Donnelly came to London from South Africa in the early 80s to work for the International Defence and Aid Fund for Southern Africa Obituary Paddy Donnelly obituary My husband, Paddy Donnelly, who has died aged 70, was a South African who moved in the early 1980s to London. There he worked for the International Defence and Aid Fund for Southern Africa (IDAF), which funded the legal costs of people tried or imprisoned for anti-apartheid activity. In addition to its legal work, the IDAF had a large archive of photographs relating to apartheid, and Paddy ran that side of the operation, processing and distributing photos of ongoing state violence to media outlets, campaigning groups and many other organisations. He was an accomplished photographer himself, and many of his photos were held in the archive. He had begun by taking pictures of townships and displaced people’s camps, and when he came to the UK he photographed anti-apartheid political meetings as well as visiting or exiled South African singers, musicians and activists.

The six-monthly HIV-prevention jab, lenacapavir, often referred to as just LEN, presented a unique challenge. "You know, lenacapavir is different. "Because we were not used to it, the practical training helped us to get used to it." She practised withdrawing the yellow liquid, using cooking oil as a stand-in. It was “now clear” that the study “will not move forward in Guinea-Bissau”, Frederik Schaltz-Buchholzer, a Danish researcher, wrote on LinkedIn, adding, “we were not given the necessary governmental approval.” The minister of health in Guinea-Bissau, Quinhin Nantote, previously denied that the project would move forward. “This is not even remotely true,” Nantote told the Guardian in Portuguese last week. The study was to be funded with $1.6m from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), along with another $1.6m from private partners like the Bill Ackman-backed Pershing Square Foundation and the Bluebell Foundation. “The solution is clear here: take the money and vaccinate as many kids as you can,” said Paul Offit, a vaccines expert at the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia, who sharply criticized the proposed study as unethical.

stories.title: Africa: African Development Bank Group Advances Sustainable Financing for Transboundary Waters At Iwc11 in Bali
stories.summary: African Development Bank Group Advances Sustainable Financing for Transboundary Waters At Iwc11 in Bali 20 October 2026 Content from a Premium Partner African Development Bank (Abidjan) announcement WHAT: African Development Bank Group participation at the 11th Global Environment Facility (GEF) Biennial International Waters Conference (IWC11) WHO: African Development Bank Group WHEN: 17-22 October 2026 WHERE: Anvaya Beach Resort, Bali, Indonesia The African Development Bank Group is participating in the 11th Global Environment Facility (GEF) Biennial International Waters Conference (IWC11), bringing its experience in financing sustainable development to global discussions on the future of transboundary waters and shared marine and freshwater ecosystems. IWC11 is taking place in Bali, Indonesia from 17 - 22 October 2026 under the theme "Shared Waters, Transformative Solutions: Enabling Systems Change." A key focus of the Bank's engagement will be sustainable financing. On 17 October, the Bank co-hosted the pre-conference workshop "From GEF Grants to Sustainable Investments: Financing the Future of Transboundary Waters and Shared Ecosystems," alongside the International Waters Learning Exchange and Resource Network (GEF IW:LEARN), the Asian Development Bank, the Development Bank of Latin America and the Caribbean, the Inter-American Development Bank and the World Bank. The workshop explored practical ways to move GEF International Waters projects beyond reliance on grant funding towards sustainable public and private investment, including blended finance and financing from multilateral development banks. During the workshop, the Bank Group led practical sessions on financing the transition to sustainable fisheries and aquaculture.

Le Bureau exécutif de la communauté a attribué ces attaques à l'organisation État islamique, selon un communiqué publié lundi.

stories.title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists
stories.summary: Image source, Reuters Image caption, El Mansouri (left) was named by King Mohammed VI (right) as the country's first female prime minister By Basma El Atti Published 20 October 2026 The Islamic saying "a people who entrust their affairs to a woman will never succeed" has resurfaced in Morocco since King Mohammed VI named Fatima Zahra El Mansouri as the country's first female prime minister. Mustafa Ramid, a former justice minister in an Islamist-led government, cited the saying earlier this month, in a lengthy Facebook post questioning whether a woman should hold the country's highest political office. He argued that Morocco, a Muslim majority country, had found a balance between equality and the responsibilities of state leadership, as the highest office - that of the king - continued to be reserved for men. Morocco operates as a constitutional monarchy. Yet executive power remains in the hands of the 63-year-old monarch.

Temporary protected status was set to end on Monday for about 101,000 Ukrainians and 1,800 Sudanese. But the DHS said an announcement “will be made at the appropriate time”.

stories.title: Au Sénégal, des appels à manifester et à une grève générale juste avant les JOJ
stories.summary: Publicité Au Sénégal, des appels à manifester et à une grève générale juste avant les JOJ Afrique Le Front syndical pour la défense du travail prévoit une marche mardi à Dakar puis trois jours de grève générale dès mercredi pour exiger l’application d’accords sur les retraites, les primes et l’indemnité logement. Le gouvernement sénégalais appelle au dialogue alors que doivent s'ouvrir, le 31 octobre, les Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse, premier événement olympique organisé en Afrique. Publié le : 19/10/2026 - 23:46 3 min Temps de lecture Partager Par : FRANCE 24 Dakar s'apprête à accueillir les Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse. © Patrick Meinhardt, AFP Un collectif de centrales syndicales au Sénégal appelle à une marche mardi 20 octobre et une grève générale à partir de mercredi 21 octobre, à quelques jours de l'ouverture au Sénégal des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) . Le Front syndical pour la défense du travail (FSDT), un collectif de treize syndicats dans divers secteurs d'activités, prévoit de manifester mardi dans la capitale sénégalaise Dakar puis de déclencher une grève générale de trois jours à partir de mercredi, a indiqué à l'AFP un de ses responsables, Elimane Diouf. Le FSDT réunit des syndicats de l'éducation, de la santé, de l'enseignement supérieur et de l'électricité, selon des responsables interrogés par l'AFP.

Cité par Reuters et AP, le bilan a été annoncé, mardi 20 octobre, par le ministre de l'Information par intérim ⁠de la région. Ce dernier accuse l'armée soudanaise d'avoir mené l'attaque dans cette ​région riche en pétrole, située à la frontière entre le Soudan du Sud et le Soudan et revendiquée par les deux pays.

stories.title: Kenyan starvation cult leader guilty of murder of 190 children and one adult
stories.summary: Doomsday preacher Paul Mackenzie during a court session of his murder trial judgment at the Mombasa law courts, Kenya on Monday. Photograph: EPA View image in fullscreen Doomsday preacher Paul Mackenzie during a court session of his murder trial judgment at the Mombasa law courts, Kenya on Monday. Photograph: EPA Kenyan starvation cult leader guilty of murder of 190 children and one adult Paul Mackenzie and his church set up sect that ordered followers to starve themselves and their children, say prosecutors A Kenyan court has found the starvation cult leader Paul Mackenzie and about 30 others guilty of murder over the deaths of ⁠190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult-related disasters in recent history. Mackenzie was arrested in 2023 after police received a tipoff, and weeks later authorities began uncovering bodies in shallow graves in the Shakahola forest near the coast ⁠in south-eastern Kenya. Prosecutors say Mackenzie and ⁠his Good News International Church organised ​a Christian doomsday sect in which they ordered followers to starve themselves and their children to death to go to heaven before the world ended.
